# Producing an answer from memory

Recognition is an unreliable rehearsal for speaking. Close the book, look at a meaning or situation, and try to supply the foreign expression before revealing it. A failed attempt followed by corrective feedback exposes what still needs practice. Saying that a sentence looks familiar is a different task.

Keep cards small enough to identify the missing knowledge. Alternate spoken and written production when both matter. An example sentence helps choose the intended sense, but should not reveal the answer through its first letters. Review outcomes should record whether the expression was produced unaided, not how pleasant the exercise felt.
